name: MI-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Moolenaar running with $1.9M cash on hand
model.rationale: Moolenaar holds a heavily Republican seat with a large financial advantage and no polling or outside spending suggesting a contest; markets price him near certain to win. Ambrose's modest fundraising gives no basis to move off the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or unexpected outside spending surge against Moolenaar would be the main way this becomes competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican John Moolenaar seeks another term in a west Michigan district that leans Republican by about fifteen points. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, roughly $1.9 million on hand, while Democrat Ben Ambrose has raised about $85,000 and has little cash remaining. No independent polls of the race are available, and no expert raters list it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Moolenaar about a 98 percent chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals and the incumbent's resources. A Green Party and an independent candidate are also on the ballot but lack visible campaigns. Absent unforeseen developments, the seat is expected to remain Republican by a wide margin.
